sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff, §17.1 in both maintained texts
sol.problem: The standing bennett-4ht check requires a change governing host memory by reference to state its mixed-fat-object use. This diff permits ordinary allocator metadata in §17.1's shared classical memory, but states obligations only for device and native materialisation. Under §17.7, native materialisation here is the comparison binary; it does not itself explain the production native host image. The proposal never states how unrelated host code remains native or how shared allocator metadata follows the existing boundary rules. Existing §§4.2–4.4, 8.5 and 19.4–19.5 provide a route, so this needs an applicability statement rather than a new ABI.
sol.fix: Append to §17.1 in both maps: 'In a mixed fat object, this bookkeeping allowance applies to runtime code in the selected materialised device closures and their native comparison build; unrelated host code remains native under §§4.2–4.4. Allocations and bookkeeping shared across the host–device boundary follow the shared-memory, promotion and layout rules of §§17.1 and 19.4–19.5, and oracle entry-state transfer under §8.5 preserves the ordinary metadata bytes as well as primitive allocation history. This clarification does not require the native host entry, argv/envp or host-only libc closure to be included in an ISA object.' Use this existing-contract route.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff — §17.1; Defect and North Star scope
codex.problem: The proposal specifies identical materialised allocator operations, actual budgets and body identities, but does not state how those obligations apply within a mixed fat object containing a native host binary and selected device closures. References to §§17.7/19.1 describe the comparison and linking paths without supplying the explicit applicability statement required by the council's standing mixed-fat-object check. This is that check's required scope omission, not a demonstrated defect in the allocation arithmetic or the accepted host/device split.
codex.fix: Append to proposed §17.1 in both maps: "In a mixed fat object, this rule governs the allocator closure selected for a marked device entry and that closure's native comparison build; the surrounding native host binary and host-only libc remain outside the device object. Allocation traces, budgets and runtime-body identities are bound to that selected closure, with shared caller allocation state transferred and charged under §8.5 and boundary addresses governed by §19.5. This clarification does not require whole-program device entry or add host promotion beyond §§4.2–4.3 and 19.4." An illustrative mixed case should retain native main and host-only work while the marked allocator-using closure produces its ISA object and comparison closure.
